sentence_stem: What puzzled the committee most was
correct_completion: why the proposal had been approved so quickly.
full_sentence: What puzzled the committee most was why the proposal had been approved so quickly.
acceptable_variants: how the proposal had been approved so quickly.
that the proposal had passed without any real debate.

options.text: the proposal had been approved so quickly.
options.why_wrong: A finite clause cannot follow 'was' directly. It needs an introducer such as 'why', 'how' or 'that' to work as a nominal clause, so this option is ungrammatical here.

options.text: so the proposal had been approved quickly.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result adverbial clause, not a nominal clause, so it cannot act as the complement of 'was'.

options.text: why the proposal had been approved so quickly.
even though the proposal had been approved so quickly.
options.why_wrong: 'Even though' introduces a concessive adverbial clause, which cannot serve as the complement of 'was'. The sentence would not answer the question set up by the stem.

grammar_focus: Nominal wh-clauses as complements in pseudo-cleft sentences
explanation: In a pseudo-cleft sentence, the part after 'was' must be a noun clause that answers the question set up by the first part. A wh-word such as 'why' introduces such a clause and can take its own subject and verb. Options with no introducer, or with a subordinator of result or concession, do not work in this position. Portuguese speakers may transfer the habit of placing a plain declarative clause directly after a linking verb, so this structure needs explicit practice.
translation: O que mais intrigou o comitê foi por que a proposta tinha sido aprovada tão rapidamente.
